evidence.observation: get_parser is the single declaration point for every CLI option and is where the input-source plumbing for the whole precedence chain is wired. It constructs a configargparse.ArgumentParser with auto_env_var_prefix="AIDER_" (so each --foo option is also accepted as the AIDER_FOO environment variable), default_config_files (the .aider.conf.yml search list), and config_file_parser_class=configargparse.YAMLConfigFileParser. It also declares -c/--config with is_config_file=True (line 788-797) so an explicit config file joins the same precedence resolution, and registers --env-file (line 800-805) as a documented default that is actually consumed by the pre-parser in main.py. Each add_argument call supplies a default= value, which is the lowest-priority source in the chain.

resolve_aiderignore_path is used as the type= callable for --aiderignore (line 426-432), rebasing a relative path against the git root at parse time. This shows that some option values are transformed during parsing rather than at the consumer, and its default (default_aiderignore_file, line 422-424) is computed from git_root, i.e. the parser's defaults themselves depend on the discovered git root passed into get_parser.

default_env_file(git_root) returns the default --env-file value (.env in the git root, else .env). This value is baked into the parser default at line 803 and is the input to main.py's load_dotenv_files, linking the CLI option layer to the dotenv layer of the precedence chain.

get_sample_yaml re-instantiates the parser with the YamlHelpFormatter and calls parse_known_args() purely so that configargparse instantiates each action.env_var value, then renders the canonical .aider.conf.yml template. It documents, in generated form, exactly which YAML keys map onto which options, confirming that config-file keys (e.g. auto-commits) are the same dests that argv and AIDER_* env vars resolve to.

main() builds default_config_files as [CWD/.aider.conf.yml, git_root/.aider.conf.yml, ~/.aider.conf.yml] (lines 464-477), parses once with parse_known_args, then reverses the list (line 494) before rebuilding the parser and parsing again (lines 496-498) so the search/merge order becomes home, git root, cwd with cwd winning. It then calls load_dotenv_files(git_root, args.env_file, args.encoding) (line 501) and finally parse_args(argv) again (line 504) so values exported from .env are visible to the second parse. This is the concrete ordering that turns the sources declared in args.py into a resolved Namespace.

load_dotenv_files loads candidate .env files with load_dotenv(..., override=True) in the order produced by generate_search_path_list, i.e. home, git root, cwd, then an explicit --env-file value, so later files overwrite earlier ones and the command-line --env-file has the highest dotenv priority. The environment is mutated before the second parse_args, which is how dotenv entries become AIDER_* env-var inputs to the parser.

generate_search_path_list encodes the lowest-to-highest priority file order used for dotenv, model-settings and model-metadata search (home, git root, cwd/project-relative, then the command-line-provided file), with de-duplication that preserves order. It is the shared ordering primitive behind the file-based sources in the precedence chain.

These lines are the runtime consumer side: the resolved Namespace fields are read directly (args.map_tokens, args.auto_commits, args.edit_format, ...) and passed as keyword arguments into Coder.create(...), after args.model/args.weak_model/args.editor_model/args.edit_format feed models.Model(...) at lines 822-826. This closes the chain: input source -> configargparse resolution -> args Namespace -> coder/model runtime behavior.

DotEnvFormatter renders each action's action.env_var as a commented #AIDER_*=<default> line, which demonstrates that configargparse attaches an env var name to every option derived from auto_env_var_prefix. The formatters (DotEnvFormatter, YamlHelpFormatter, MarkdownHelpFormatter) are the documentation surface that mirrors the same option/env/config triple.

claims.claim: aider/args.py declares every option exactly once in get_parser, and creating the parser with auto_env_var_prefix="AIDER_" makes each option simultaneously available from three input sources that configargparse resolves in the order defaults < config file < AIDER_* environment variable < command-line argv.

The config-file source is .aider.conf.yml resolved through -c/--config (is_config_file=True) plus the default_config_files list; main.py first parses with search order cwd/git-root/home, then reverses that list to home -> git root -> cwd before the final parse, so a config file closer to the working directory wins when the same key (e.g. auto-commits) is set in more than one file.

.env files are a fourth source that is injected between parse passes: load_dotenv_files loads home/.env, git-root/.env, cwd/.env and then any --env-file (default from args.py's default_env_file) with override=True, so the explicit --env-file wins among dotenv files and the resulting AIDER_* variables are picked up by the second parser.parse_args(argv) call.

Config/CLI defaults declared in aider/args.py are not the final word: the parser's defaults are themselves computed from environment state (git_root for --aiderignore and --env-file), and some values are transformed at parse time by type= callables such as resolve_aiderignore_path, so the 'default' rung of the precedence chain is context-dependent.

The resolved argparse Namespace is the runtime contract: main.py reads args.model/args.weak_model/args.editor_model/args.edit_format into models.Model and passes args.auto_commits, args.map_tokens, args.auto_lint, args.stream, args.detect_urls, etc. into Coder.create, so whichever source won the precedence contest directly determines coder behavior.

conclusion: In aider, option/config precedence is implemented as a layered chain owned by aider/args.py: get_parser declares each option once with a default and sets auto_env_var_prefix="AIDER_", so configargparse can resolve the same option from defaults, YAML config files, AIDER_* environment variables, and argv. main.py supplies the ordering: it collects default_config_files as cwd/.aider.conf.yml, git-root/.aider.conf.yml and ~/.aider.conf.yml, parses once, reverses the list (home -> git root -> cwd) and re-parses so the nearest .aider.conf.yml wins; -c/--config with is_config_file=True injects an explicit config file at the top of that layer. Between the two parse passes it calls load_dotenv_files, which loads home, git root, cwd and finally the --env-file value with override=True, exporting AIDER_* variables that the final parser.parse_args(argv) then reads; argv itself overrides everything. The resulting Namespace is consumed by models.Model and Coder.create in main.py, so a change's effective value can be traced source -> configargparse -> args Namespace -> runtime consumer. Config-file priority is home < git root < cwd; dotenv priority is home < git root < cwd < --env-file; and both sit below argv in the overall chain.
